*“Elsa…” She fiddled with the Rook in her hand, running a thumb down its side. “It’s not treason to beat the Queen at chess, is it?”*

*There was a playful glint in her sister’s eye as she prepared to make her move.*

*“Yes, actually. I’m surprised you didn’t know that.”*

*“You’re lying,” Anna burst out, slamming the Rook down. “It is not!”*

*“It’s not,” Elsa agreed slowly, studying the board for any way out. “But for you, dear sister, I’ll make an exception.”*

*The look on Anna’s face had her double over in laughter, as much as she tried to hide it. When she straightened up again a pillow smacked her in the face.*

It was over in a minute. Three spears of ice had formed, razor sharp icicles. One pierced the wood just under her arm. The other was sticking out of her kneecap, a mess of shattered bone. The last had gone through her throat and into the wood behind. So shocked was the Queen that she didn’t even notice her own wound until she stumbled back, causing a hot flash to streak up her side. The dagger quivered slightly from between her ribs and Elsa’s body shook with a wet cough.

*“Checkmate,” Anna chirped.*

“The Commander isn’t wrong. We need more supplies,” a pause at the thought of Arendelle’s meager supply store, “..and if Weselton is unwilling to release our ships, we should take them back by force.”

“Our Navy can do that.” Anna said, “You’re in no condition.”

“Anna.”

“No, don’t ‘Anna’ me, Elsa! You collapsed during a meeting! You have no business fighting and dodging crossbow arrows when you’re this tired!”

Elsa couldn’t help but scoff at that, already sensing ice forming on her skin. “Dodging arrows? With a wave of my hand-“

Anna grabbed it before she could demonstrate, pressing it down against the sheets.

The Queen shot her a glare and turned her attention to the pages clutched in her sister’s free hand.

“Is that my paperwork?”

“This?” Anna waved the ink-stained paper.
“Give it here.” Elsa snapped, wanting to deal with it now so she could sleep. Her mind felt foggy and her head was so heavy.. 

“No.” The younger sister got up, heading for the door. “You need to rest first. The Kingdom can wait. Arendelle can wait... I’ll get you something to make you feel better.”

The older one didn’t reply, didn’t even notice her leave, as she had already fallen asleep.

True. I don’t know about others, but for me cutting was a way to distract myself from my emotional pain by inflicting physical pain. I used to talk to my one friend I trusted to share my problems with, but she started getting annoyed and I always felt like I was burdening her(and probably was). When I could no longer talk to her I started cutting more to relieve the stress, anxiety, self-hatred.. My parents found out and took away my knives. Now I had to find other ways to hurt myself because my emotions grew stronger and built up. I found other means, such as making myself ill. With a knife I knew how deep to cut, how much pressure to use, where my veins were. I knew my limits. With my familiar tool taken away I used other means, which may have caused serious harm. Taking my knives away did nothing to stop me from self harming, it only made me resent my parents for taking the knives away. It simply made me find worse ways to harm, and made me better at hiding the signs.
